purpose: Ampicillin is used to treat bacterial infections in many parts of your body, including your ears, lungs, urinary tract, skin, and stomach. It can also help fight more serious infections like meningitis. It only works against bacteria — it will not help with colds, flu, or other viral infections.
how_it_works: Ampicillin works by attacking the outer wall that surrounds bacteria. Without a strong wall, the bacteria fall apart and die. Think of it like knocking down the protective shell that keeps the bacteria alive — once it is gone, the infection cannot survive.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects are an upset stomach, nausea, diarrhea, and a skin rash. You may also notice a sore mouth or tongue. Most of these are mild and go away on their own, but let your doctor or pharmacist know if they bother you.
warnings: Tell your doctor right away if you develop a severe rash, hives, swelling of your face or throat, or have trouble breathing, as these could be signs of a serious allergic reaction. If you are allergic to penicillin or cephalosporin antibiotics, do not take ampicillin. Taking it when you do not need it can make antibiotics less effective over time, so always finish the full course even if you feel better.
typical_dosing: For most adults, the usual dose is 250 mg to 500 mg taken by mouth every 6 hours, meaning four times a day. Your doctor may prescribe a different dose depending on your specific infection and how serious it is. Always take it exactly as prescribed and try to take it on an empty stomach for the best results.
